title: Equilibrium angles identified
description: Essential: The student must state the four equilibrium angles where α is constant: 0, π, π/2, and 3π/2 radians.

title: Equation of motion derived
description: Important: The student's solution must show the derivation of the simplified equation of motion leading to the condition sin(α)cos(α) = 0.

title: Energy change calculated
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the change in orbital energy as ΔU = (1/2) m Ω² R ΔR.

title: Work-energy balance applied
description: Essential: The student must equate the work done by the Lorentz force (B I L v t) to the calculated change in orbital energy.

title: Final time computed
description: Essential: The student must provide the final numerical answer for the required time, approximately 5.8 × 10³ s.

title: Orbital velocity used
description: Important: The student must correctly relate the orbital speed v to the given period T or angular speed Ω (v = ΩR).

title: Sign error in current
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses the wrong sign for the applied current relative to the induced current, or misapplies the Lorentz force direction.

title: Approximation justification
description: Optional: The student notes the use of the small-L approximation (L << R) to simplify the gravitational force expansion.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The student demonstrates unit analysis for the final time calculation, confirming seconds as the unit.
